solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pact I arranged for everyone behind surrender

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of 'Pact I' are put into a new order

parts.note: U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal, suitable for everyone
behind, as in behind schedule, means late

explanation.surface: Someone describes signing a treaty that means everyone gives in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' here means late, as running behind schedule; U is the British film certificate for films suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: To capitulate is to yield or give in, a straightforward verb synonym of surrender.

clue.text: Nearly stick up a shrub

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to cock is to stick up or raise, as a dog cocks its ears

explanation.surface: Almost holding up a bush, as in a hold-up at a hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: Coca is the South American bush whose leaves yield cocaine, so it is an example of a shrub.

clue.text: Roughly pin elm around each flower

indicators.note: around means the anagrammed letters wrap round the next piece
roughly means the letters of 'pin elm' are treated loosely and rearranged

parts.note: per means each, as in a pound per person

explanation.surface: A gardener loosely arranges a pin and elm around every bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' turns PIN ELM into PIMNEL, which goes 'around' PER.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet pimpernel is a small wild plant with red blooms, so an example of a flower.

clue.text: Figure of speech appears in intro, perhaps

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A rhetorical device turns up in someone's introduction, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figurative use of language such as metaphor, a rhetorical device.

clue.text: Back trouble's to delay oxygen without university medic

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the first pieces wrap round the rest

parts.note: to lag is to delay or fall behind
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical degree, so a doctor
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A bad back makes someone put off breathing gas without seeing a college doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: LAGO wraps round UMB.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the lower back, a kind of back trouble.

clue.text: Roar at end of fight with barbarian overcoming the German

indicators.note: overcoming in a down clue means the barbarian sits on top of the German article
at end of means take the final letter of fight

parts.note: the Huns were a nomadic people taken as the archetypal barbarians
der is German for the

explanation.surface: A war cry after a battle in which a savage defeats a German.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunder is a loud rumbling roar, as in the roar of a storm.

clue.text: Alliance with second-rate colonel retreating

parts.note: B is second class, next after A

indicators.note: retreating means the abbreviation runs backwards in an across answer

explanation.surface: A coalition including a mediocre colonel who is pulling back.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or parties combined for a common purpose, an alliance.

clue.text: Caught in temptation for money

indicators.note: in means the cricket abbreviation goes inside the word for temptation

parts.note: a lure is an enticement or temptation
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone trapped by the lure of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, usually with the sense of ill-gotten gain, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: Annoyed by coffees he'd ruined

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of 'coffees he'd' are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone irritated because the coffees he made were spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cheesed off is British slang for being irritated or fed up.

clue.text: Do nothing with fly in food that's returned

indicators.note: in means the insect goes inside the reversed word
returned means the word for food is read backwards

parts.note: eats is an informal word for food
a gnat is a small fly

explanation.surface: A diner refuses to act when an insect turns up in a meal sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns EATS into STAE, and GNAT goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stay inactive and make no progress, to do nothing.

clue.text: Brief appearance is shut out from what follows, oddly

indicators.note: out from means the letters of shut are taken away from the longer word
oddly means the letters left over are rearranged

parts.note: what follows is the answer to the next clue, 11 across, MOUSTACHE

explanation.surface: An actor's short walk-on is excluded from the next scene, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what follows' points to 11 across: take S, H, U, T 'out from' MOUSTACHE, leaving MOACE, which 'oddly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a small but notable part played by a well-known performer, a short appearance.

clue.text: Rodent outside entrance to hole after cat comes back for something hairy

indicators.note: outside means the rodent wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a mouse is a small rodent

indicators.note: after puts the hole's first letter behind the reversed cat
comes back means the word cat is read backwards
entrance to means the first letter of hole

explanation.surface: A mouse runs round a hole as a cat returns, with something furry involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something hairy' is a deliberately vague definition; the cat reverses and the hole gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair grown on the upper lip is a fair, deliberately vague description: something hairy.

clue.text: Ambassador's prize for old English hero

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title given to an ambassador
a reward is a prize

explanation.surface: An envoy receives an award honouring an Anglo-Saxon champion.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereward the Wake led English resistance to the Norman Conquest in the Fens.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereward the Wake was an eleventh-century Anglo-Saxon rebel against the Normans, a historical hero.

clue.text: Visitor doesn't finish with second opinion

indicators.note: doesn't finish means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: A caller leaves early, then someone seeks another doctor's view.
explanation.definitionFit: A guess is an opinion formed without full evidence, an estimate.

clue.text: Thoroughly cleaned tile dries out after a bit of soaking

indicators.note: after places the anagram behind the single letter
a bit of means just the first letter of soaking
out means the letters of 'tile dries' are put out of order

explanation.surface: A tile is scrubbed and left to dry after soaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TILE DRIES into TERILISED, which comes 'after' S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterilised describes something made free of germs, so cleaned thoroughly.

clue.text: Fruit's distinctive taste — peeled melon

parts.note: a tang is a sharp distinctive flavour

indicators.note: peeled means the outer letters of melon are removed

explanation.surface: A fruit with a sharp flavour, like a melon without its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo, so a fruit.

clue.text: Skilfully dismiss outside right with ultimate in trickery

indicators.note: outside means the verb for dismiss surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: to expel is to dismiss or throw out

indicators.note: ultimate in means the last letter of trickery

explanation.surface: A conjuror deftly sends off a right-wing heckler with the last of his tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertly means with expert skill, an adverb synonym of skilfully.

clue.text: Cooked ginger without large oven

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the colour wraps round the kiln

parts.note: ginger hair is red
an oast is a large kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: Food is prepared with no ginger and no big oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking. An OAST is a hop-drying kiln, common in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: To be roasted is to be cooked in dry heat in an oven.

clue.text: Moment of time with suspicion

parts.note: an inkling is a vague suspicion or hint

explanation.surface: A brief moment while someone harbours a suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word between the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In the twinkling of an eye, a twinkling is an instant or very short moment.

clue.text: Put back trellis I left to deteriorate

indicators.note: put back means the remaining letters are written in reverse
left means the letter I has departed from the word

parts.note: an espalier is a trellis on which fruit trees are trained flat
I is taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener replaces a trellis left to rot.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing I from ESPALIER leaves ESPALER, which 'Put back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into a worse state, to deteriorate again.

clue.text: Historic old chapel destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An ancient chapel has been razed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' gives only O; it joins CHAPEL in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Epochal means marking an epoch, so momentous or historic.

clue.text: Fresh changes embracing condition of law officer

indicators.note: embracing means the anagrammed letters wrap round the condition
changes means the letters of fresh are rearranged

parts.note: if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: New reforms covering the state of a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like an adjective but is the anagram fodder; 'condition' is the conditional word, not a state.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheriff is a county law-enforcement official, in the US chiefly.

clue.text: For example, flat screen's manufactured badly — first four components missing

indicators.note: manufactured means the letters of screen are made into something new

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

indicators.note: first four components missing means the opening four letters of badly are removed

explanation.surface: A flat-screen TV is badly made with its first four parts gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' is not a TV: a flat is a painted canvas frame used as theatre scenery. Removing BADL leaves Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre flat is a painted frame forming part of a stage set, so one item of the setting.

clue.text: One extant organ

definitions.meaning: one who is extant, still alive, is someone who lives
a large glandular organ in the abdomen

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, one who lives is a liver, and the liver is also a vital internal organ.

clue.text: One struggling, apparently, gripping head of poisonous snake

indicators.note: gripping means the outer word holds the letter inside

parts.note: a vier is one who vies, so a competitor in a struggle; apparently flags the made-up noun

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of poisonous

explanation.surface: Someone fighting seizes a venomous serpent by the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A viper is a venomous snake such as the adder.

clue.text: Pass extra assessment

parts.note: over means extra or left over
a take is a view or assessment, as in your take on it

explanation.surface: Getting through by means of a supplementary test.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtake is to pass a vehicle going the same way.

clue.text: Drinker's drunk 3

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are reeling, out of order

parts.note: 3 refers to the answer to 3 down, TROPE

explanation.surface: A tippler is plastered, as the cross-reference says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges the letters of TROPE, the answer to 3 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A toper is a habitual heavy drinker.

clue.text: See heads of state preside over talks

indicators.note: heads of means the first letters of the next four words

explanation.surface: Watch the leaders of a nation chair negotiations.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot is to see or notice something.

clue.text: Maybe cheers up around the third part of pole vault

indicators.note: around means the anagram wraps round the single letter
maybe suggests the letters of 'cheers up' could be rearranged
the third part of means the third letter of pole

explanation.surface: Spectators perhaps cheer the third attempt in a pole-vault event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges CHEERS UP into SEPUCHRE, which goes 'around' L. 'vault' is not the athletics event but a burial chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepulchre is a tomb or burial chamber, which a vault also is.

clue.text: Page follows formal groom

indicators.note: follows puts the abbreviation for page after the adjective

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and proper

explanation.surface: A pageboy walks behind a formal bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to groom oneself fussily, as groom is used as a verb.

clue.text: Terrible one adding colour for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a dyer is one who adds colour to cloth

explanation.surface: An awful person colours things in front of spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means dreadful or terrible.

clue.text: Dramatist's predicament involving awkward way to finish off actor

indicators.note: involving means the word for predicament takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a plight is a predicament or difficult situation

indicators.note: awkward means the letters of way are put clumsily out of order
finish off means the final letter of actor

explanation.surface: A playwright is in a fix, needing an awkward way to dispatch an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way to finish off actor' reads like killing a character, but it is WAY scrambled plus the last letter of actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A playwright is a writer of plays, so a dramatist.
